page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores based on the ARM64 architecture, specifically the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory subsystem performance, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 363.94 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 182.89 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. The instance also demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance in Geekbench and Passmark database operations. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES instructions, though x86-specific instruction sets like AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are absent.

While the instance excels in memory-intensive operations, database tasks, and multi-threaded decompression, it exhibits performance limitations on larger workloads. Specifically, LLM inference prompt processing for a large 70B model is weak, registering at 5.9 tokens/sec, though text generation for the same model remains average. The combination of dedicated ARM64 cores, high memory bandwidth, and local NVMe storage makes this instance highly cost-efficient for database operations, static web serving, Redis deployments, and software compilation, rather than heavy large-scale AI model inference.
